title.sl: Več oziralnih stavkov: who z vejico, whose, whom
title.de: Mehr Relativsätze: who mit Komma, whose, whom
title.it: Altre relative: who con la virgola, whose, whom
title.en: More relative clauses: who with commas, whose, whom

rule.sl:
Stavek **z vejicama** doda nekaj o osebi ali stvari, ki jo že poznaš: **Mr Dixon, who lives by the beck, is our blacksmith.** Če ga izpustiš, še vedno veš, kdo je. Brez vejic pove, katera oseba: **the man who lives by the beck**. Slovenščina ima vejico v obeh.

Zato: **Edna's son, who lives in Keswick** (en sin); **Edna's son who lives in Keswick** (več sinov).

Za vejico se piše **who**, **which**, **whose**; *that* ostane za stavke brez vejic. Tudi kot predmet beseda ostane: **Hill Top, which we visited last year, is in Near Sawrey.**

**whose** je his, her, its, their: **Old Wilf, whose dog died last year, lives alone.**

V govoru predlog ostane na koncu: **Mr Tyson, who I spoke to**. V uradnem pisanju gre naprej: **Mr Tyson, to whom I spoke**, **the house in which she lives**. Ljudje rečejo tudi *to who*; pisno je **whom**.

**which** se lahko nanaša na cel stavek, kot *kar*: **The van broke down, which was a pity.** Ljudje rečejo tudi *what was a pity*; pisno je **which**. Za most of, both of: **forty sheep, most of which are Herdwicks**, **two sons, both of whom live in Kendal**.
rule.de:
Ein Satz **mit Kommas** fügt etwas über jemanden hinzu, den du schon kennst: **Mr Dixon, who lives by the beck, is our blacksmith.** Lässt du ihn weg, weißt du noch, wer es ist. Ohne Kommas sagt er, welche Person: **the man who lives by the beck**. Deutsch hat in beiden ein Komma.

Also: **Edna's son, who lives in Keswick** (ein Sohn); **Edna's son who lives in Keswick** (mehrere Söhne).

Nach dem Komma steht geschrieben **who**, **which**, **whose**; *that* bleibt für Sätze ohne Kommas. Auch als Objekt bleibt das Wort: **Hill Top, which we visited last year, is in Near Sawrey.**

**whose** ist his, her, its, their: **Old Wilf, whose dog died last year, lives alone.**

Gesprochen bleibt die Präposition am Ende: **Mr Tyson, who I spoke to**. Förmlich steht sie vorn: **Mr Tyson, to whom I spoke**, **the house in which she lives**. Man sagt auch *to who*; geschrieben steht **whom**.

**which** kann für einen ganzen Satz stehen, wie deutsch was: **The van broke down, which was a pity.** Man sagt auch *what was a pity*; geschrieben steht **which**. Nach most of, both of: **forty sheep, most of which are Herdwicks**, **two sons, both of whom live in Kendal**.
rule.it:
Una frase **con le virgole** aggiunge qualcosa su chi conosci già: **Mr Dixon, who lives by the beck, is our blacksmith.** Se la togli, sai ancora chi è. Senza virgole dice quale persona: **the man who lives by the beck**.

Quindi: **Edna's son, who lives in Keswick** (un figlio); **Edna's son who lives in Keswick** (più figli).

Dopo la virgola, per iscritto, si usa **who**, **which**, **whose**; *that* resta per le frasi senza virgole. Anche come oggetto la parola resta: **Hill Top, which we visited last year, is in Near Sawrey.**

**whose** è his, her, its, their: **Old Wilf, whose dog died last year, lives alone.**

A voce la preposizione resta in fondo: **Mr Tyson, who I spoke to**. Nello scritto formale va davanti: **Mr Tyson, to whom I spoke**, **the house in which she lives**. Si dice anche *to who*; per iscritto si usa **whom**.

**which** può stare per una frase intera, come *il che*: **The van broke down, which was a pity.** Si dice anche *what was a pity*; per iscritto si usa **which**. Dopo most of, both of: **forty sheep, most of which are Herdwicks**, **two sons, both of whom live in Kendal**.
rule.en:
A clause **with commas** adds something about someone or something you already know: **Mr Dixon, who lives by the beck, is our blacksmith.** Take it out and you still know who. With no commas it says which person: **the man who lives by the beck**.

So: **Edna's son, who lives in Keswick** (one son); **Edna's son who lives in Keswick** (more than one).

After a comma writing wants **who**, **which**, **whose**; *that* stays for clauses with no commas. Even as the object the word stays: **Hill Top, which we visited last year, is in Near Sawrey.**

**whose** is his, her, its, their: **Old Wilf, whose dog died last year, lives alone.**

In talk the small word stays at the end: **Mr Tyson, who I spoke to**. Formal writing puts it first: **Mr Tyson, to whom I spoke**, **the house in which she lives**. People also say *to who*; writing wants **whom**.

**which** can stand for a whole sentence: **The van broke down, which was a pity.** People also say *what was a pity*; writing wants **which**. After most of, both of: **forty sheep, most of which are Herdwicks**, **two sons, both of whom live in Kendal**.

rule.sl: Z vejicama: še nekaj o znanem: **Mr Dixon, who lives by the beck, …** Brez vejic: kateri: **the man who lives by the beck**. Za vejico **who, which, whose**. Uradno: **to whom**, **in which**. Cel stavek: **…, which was a pity.**
rule.de: Mit Kommas: noch etwas über Bekanntes: **Mr Dixon, who lives by the beck, …** Ohne Kommas: welcher: **the man who lives by the beck**. Nach dem Komma **who, which, whose**. Förmlich: **to whom**, **in which**. Ganzer Satz: **…, which was a pity.**
rule.it: Con le virgole: altro su chi è noto: **Mr Dixon, who lives by the beck, …** Senza virgole: quale: **the man who lives by the beck**. Dopo la virgola **who, which, whose**. Formale: **to whom**, **in which**. Frase intera: **…, which was a pity.**
rule.en: With commas: more about someone known: **Mr Dixon, who lives by the beck, …** No commas: which one: **the man who lives by the beck**. After a comma **who, which, whose**. Formal: **to whom**, **in which**. A whole sentence: **…, which was a pity.**

tip.sl: 💡 Slovenščina piše vejico vedno: **the man who lives here** je brez nje. *kar* = **which**.
tip.de: 💡 Deutsch setzt immer ein Komma: **the man who lives here** hat keines. *was* = **which**.
tip.it: 💡 *che* va dappertutto: dopo la virgola **who** o **which**. *il che* = **which**.
tip.en: 💡 A name already says who: commas. **The man who lives here** has none.
